12 days ago, Jensen Huang quit Nvidia. Today he's back.
Nov 8: he admitted an affair and apologized.
Nov 12: he resigned after 33 years. Stock fell up to 14%.
By Friday: $125.53, down nearly 50% from October.
Why bring him back? The board cites his candor and ability to lead.
After U.S. government input: no national security risk, the board says.
Wall Street's verdict: up 30%+ this morning.
Smart move, or a risk they'll regret?
